_comment: Game-day scenarios for scripts/game-day.ps1 (Phase 9, docs/18). inject.kind: chaos = a Chaos Mesh file in infra/chaos/, faults = --set-json faults.* on a release. expect.* are regexes (case-insensitive) the run's root cause must match - a crude, honest eval: a human still reads the reports.

scenarios.name: pod-kill-orders-api
scenarios.hypothesis: Killing 1 of 3 orders-api pods is invisible to users: the frontend SLI stays under 1%, no agent needed.

scenarios.name: error-rate-orders-api
scenarios.hypothesis: 30% of orders-api requests fail with 500. The agent blames orders-api itself (not the database), and a restart does not help because the fault is in the running code/config.
scenarios.note: users report errors on the site

scenarios.name: network-delay-postgres
scenarios.hypothesis: +300 ms on postgres answers burns the orders-api latency SLO; the agent names the database (latency), not orders-api, and proposes no restart.
scenarios.note: users report that the site is slow

scenarios.name: memory-leak-orders-api
scenarios.hypothesis: A 60 MB/min leak gets orders-api pods OOMKilled one by one; the agent finds OOMKilled + memory growth. A restart only buys time.

scenarios.name: cpu-stress-orders-api
scenarios.hypothesis: False alarm: CPU stress makes orders-api throttled at its 500m limit, but (measured: 100% throttled periods, 0% slow requests at ~5 rps) users are not affected. The agent should see that the SLIs are fine and propose no action.
scenarios.note: users report that the site is slow
